page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. This instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES and VAES cryptography, SHA_NI, and hypervisor virtualization. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2684.89. However, multi-core performance is weak, scoring 2695.68 in stress-ng and 1813.0 in Geekbench, both falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory performance is constrained, with a Passmark memory score of 1007.44 and a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 125.99 GB/sec, which are categorized in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 25.91 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.87 GB/sec perform at average levels.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-2 is its low memory allocation of 2.0 GB relative to its 2 vCPUs, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This resource profile represents a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require substantial memory or local storage. Due to poor multi-core scaling, poor database operations performance of 906.95 on Passmark, and low static web serving throughput of 2.41 GB/sec, this instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic text processing, and simple utility scripting rather than heavy database hosting, large-scale web serving, or complex multi-threaded compilations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-focused server configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, 1 physical core, and 2.0 GB of system memory. It features no local storage and no bundled GPUs. The instance exhibits strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks, placing in the top 25%, but shows weak multi-core scaling and poor memory bandwidth. With only 1.0 GB of RAM per core and a low Passmark memory score, this server is constrained for memory-heavy or highly parallelized tasks. It represents a cost-efficient entry point for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, and simple utility scripts that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory and storage demands.
